page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the instance delivers modest compute performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show poor performance, falling into the bottom 10%. However, large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations perform at an average level, as do Passmark CPU extended instruction and physics tests. Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference tasks also achieve average throughput, though larger model inference speeds are poor.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.2xlarge is its high memory capacity paired with relatively weak processing capabilities. This resource density makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require substantial memory footprints but do not demand intensive CPU cycles. It is suitable for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, medium-sized databases, and lightweight data processing pipelines, while being less optimal for compute-heavy tasks like software compilation, complex cryptography, or large-scale machine learning inference.
